name: comparator-regeneration
description: Decision time versus input overdrive over PVT at 50 mV / 1 mV / 0.1 mV, the regeneration time constant tau extracted from the two small rungs, the near-metastable behaviour at 0.1 mV, and the switching energy and static current per decision.
claim: PLACEHOLDER DUT. sim/dut.json binds sim/dut/placeholder_comparator.spice (id placeholder-v1, provenance placeholder). This record substantiates the harness -- that a three-overdrive transient regeneration sweep genuinely runs and tau is genuinely extracted from it over the full PVT grid -- and is NOT evidence toward README.md#target-specification's Decision-time-vs-overdrive row until design/comparator.sch exists and sim/dut.json is repointed at it (spec/porting-plan.md next step 1).
analyses: meas tran vsup_v find v(vdd) at=25n
meas tran td_a trig v(clkn) val=0.5 rise=2 targ v(dan) val=0.5 rise=1 td=35n
meas tran td_b trig v(clkn) val=0.5 rise=2 targ v(dbn) val=0.5 rise=1 td=35n
meas tran td_c trig v(clkn) val=0.5 rise=2 targ v(dcn) val=0.5 rise=1 td=35n
meas tran da_first find v(dan) at=18n
meas tran db_first find v(dbn) at=18n
meas tran dc_first find v(dcn) at=18n
meas tran da_end find v(dan) at=55n
meas tran db_end find v(dbn) at=55n
meas tran dc_end find v(dcn) at=55n
meas tran i_stat avg i(vsupa) from=25n to=29n
meas tran q_dec integ i(vsupa) from=39.9n to=48n

td_od50_ns.description: PRIMARY CORNER-SENSITIVITY ANCHOR as well as the row-facing number. The min/max pair is a sanity envelope, not the spec bound: 1 ps would mean the delay measurement latched onto a numerical artefact, and 25 ns is most of the strobe window. The SPEC bound (README.md's decision-time row) is deliberately NOT encoded while sim/dut.json binds a placeholder. The per-axis floors are what make --sabotage-corners fail: regeneration speed is set by device transconductance, which is corner- and temperature-sensitive. Floors calibrated from this experiment's first committed 45-point record (named in this experiment's README.md, run --no-write during issue #8 development), with ~40% margin below the observed weakest slices (process 2.61%, temperature 12.76%). The supply axis is unfloored because the delay threshold is supply-normalized on purpose (see the deck header), which removes most of the supply dependence from the measurement by construction (observed weakest supply slice: 2.02%).

tau_ps.description: Regeneration time constant, extracted from the (1 mV, 0.1 mV) pair -- both inside the logarithmic region, one decade apart, so tau = (t(0.1 mV) - t(1 mV))/ln(10). Bounds are a sanity envelope: a negative or sub-0.1 ps tau means the two delays came out in the wrong order, and 20 ns means the structure is not regenerating on the timescale of the strobe.

resolve_decades.description: How many e-folds of regeneration fit inside the measured 1 mV decision time (td_od1 / tau). It is the metastability lever arm: the probability of an unresolved decision falls as exp(-t/tau), so this is the exponent that number is taken to.

dout_od50_end.description: POLARITY CHECK: after the second strobe the 50 mV instance must hold the POSITIVE answer (dout normalized to its own supply). Together with dout_od50_first below it proves the same instance decided BOTH ways within one run.

dout_od01_end.description: the same at 0.1 mV overdrive -- i.e. the near-metastable rung still resolves to the CORRECT answer within the strobe window, which is the statement the metastability row rests on.

dout_od50_first.description: the OPPOSITE-polarity half of the same proof: at the first strobe the input was negative, so the held output must be low.

i_static_ua.description: Static supply current of one instance with the strobe low. A floor only: zero would mean the bias never came up and every dynamic number in this record was taken on a dead circuit.

notes: MISMATCH-FREE BY CONSTRUCTION (the plain mos corner set). Regeneration time and offset are separable effects and are budgeted separately.
THE DELAY IS MEASURED ON THE SECOND STROBE, where the output must actively flip a latch holding the opposite answer.
TIMING THRESHOLDS ARE SUPPLY-NORMALIZED (each output divided by its own supply, crossed at 0.5).
METASTABILITY IS A FIRST-CLASS ROW HERE, not a note. tau and resolve_decades are recorded at every PVT point.

e_dec_fj CARRIES NO CHECK, DELIBERATELY. The placeholder DUT's decision stage is behavioural and draws no supply current at all, so the switching energy measured here is the FRONT END's alone and what remains of the charge integral is dominated by numerical residue. A check belongs here the moment a transistor-level decision stage is bound in sim/dut.json.

THE TARG SEARCHES START AT td=35n, PORTED FROM gf180-comparator's fix (its own PR history): a real comparator's output SR latch has no defined power-up state, so an unwindowed targ search can lock onto the t=0 metastable-resolution transient instead of the strobe-driven decision under test. 35 ns is after the first strobe has completed and after the 20 ns input flip has settled, and before the second strobe at 40 ns.

SOLVER TOLERANCES. reltol = 1e-4 and vntol = 1e-9 are tightened from the ngspice defaults so that a sub-nanosecond delay difference between two overdrives is resolved rather than smeared. abstol is 1e-13, matching gf180-comparator's finding that 1e-15 (the kickback deck's tighter setting) makes some points of this grid fail to take their first transient step at all.
